findings.summary: Typo in code example makes the brace-init example invalid.
findings.evidence: Prefer brace init int x{5]; auto when obvious
findings.fix: Change to int x{5}; and split the line into two bullets (brace init; auto when obvious).

findings.summary: Bullet on constexpr is split across fragments, so the reasoning is hard to follow.
findings.evidence: constexpr also needs a compile-time value / So it can size arrays: constexpr int N = 8; int a[N];
findings.fix: Merge into one line: 'constexpr: value known at compile time, so it can size arrays' with the code on its own line.

findings.summary: The 'Common Mistakes' bullet packs a rule and its example into one line.
findings.evidence: -1 < 1u is false: the signed value converts to unsigned
findings.fix: Split into the rule 'mixed signed/unsigned comparison converts signed to unsigned' and the example '-1 < 1u is false'.

findings.summary: Code is shown before the one-line idea, and one bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: sizeof(p) is 8 bytes on 64-bit; a reference has no address of its own
findings.fix: State the idea first ('& takes an address, * dereferences') above the code, and split the sizeof bullet into two bullets.

findings.summary: Code shown before its idea is stated, and one bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: Trailing elements zeroed only with an initializer list
findings.fix: Put the one-line idea 'decay loses the size' before the code block, and clarify the zeroing bullet (e.g. 'int a[5]{} zeroes all').

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "mismatching", "dangling").
findings.evidence: Mistakes: memory leak (new without delete), double delete, use-after-free (p stays dangling, so set p = nullptr after delete), and mismatching new[] with delete
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The pipeline and mistakes are written as a prose-like bullet list where a table would scan better.
findings.evidence: Leak (new without delete), double delete, use-after-free (set p = nullptr), new[] with delete.
findings.fix: Use a Mistake | Fix table: leak -> delete or RAII, double delete -> nullptr after delete, use-after-free -> nullptr, new[] with delete -> delete[].

findings.summary: ODR and RAII are used without being expanded or explained anywhere in the chapter.
findings.evidence: Page 5: "non-inline function defined in header (ODR)"; page 4: "3. RAII and Mistakes" and "How to avoid leaks? RAII: unique_ptr, vector"
findings.fix: Expand ODR as 'One Definition Rule: each function may be defined only once across the program'. Add a one-line RAII definition on page 4: 'resource lifetime is tied to a scope, so the destructor frees it automatically'.

findings.summary: Bullet mixes two ideas and the overload-ambiguity example is crammed into a table cell.
findings.evidence: Tie | Ambiguity error | f(5) with f(long), f(double)
findings.fix: Move the ambiguity case into its own bullet with the explanation 'int to long and int to double are both conversions'.
